paragraphs.text: Old Rainbow is a loose [raw pu’er](sheng:identity) from Yunnan, the counterpart to the shop's New Rainbow. The village or mountain behind the leaf is not known.

The leaf was made in the raw way. Large-leaf tea is picked, withered and fried in a wok, then rolled and dried in the sun, giving [maocha](sheng:making). It is never hot-air dried, so some of the leaf's own activity survives, and that is why the tea keeps [changing through storage](sheng:aging), year after year. This lot was [left loose](sheng:processing) rather than pressed.

brewing.text: Young raw pu’er takes water a little off the boil, about 85 to 95°C, because hotter water draws out more of its bitterness; an aged one takes 95°C to boiling. A common start is about 7 grams to 100 ml and a quick rinse of a few seconds, then a first steep of ten to fifteen seconds, adding a few seconds each round. A good raw tea gives eight to ten cups or more.

notice.text: In young raw pu’er, a bitter, drying bite that turns into a returning sweetness, a feel in the throat that makes the mouth water, and fresh, floral or fruity notes such as apricot or plum. Tea kept in humid storage can carry a damp, earthy storage taste.
